N + s -> z. Same nasal voicing as sanbyaku, different consonant.

THE MYRIAD BREAK. Japanese regroups every FOUR digits, not three. 10,000 is ichiman, never *juusen. And the ichi is obligatory: never bare *man. 100,000 = juuman, 1,000,000 = hyakuman.

4 morae: sa-N-ni-N. Two separate nasal beats; do not merge them.
THE REAL IRREGULAR. yo-nin, 3 morae. NOT *yonnin, NOT *yonin with a doubled n. Compare yoji, which drops the n the same way.

4 morae: na-N-ni-N.

No gemination: rokuji, not *rokkuji.
LEXICALIZED EXCEPTION: the shichi form is required. *nanaji is not said (nanaji is heard occasionally for clarity but do not produce it).
LEXICALIZED EXCEPTION: ku-ji, never *kyuuji. Two morae only.

kana: のみ、たべ、まち、はなし、し、き
gloss: the shelf every non-te ending hangs on
audioText: nomi, tabe, machi, hanashi, shi, ki
note: THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE MOVE IN THE COURSE. Named HERE because it is free: it is already the -masu stem the learner is about to drill 500 times. Formation: ichidan drop -ru (tabe-); godan -u to -i (nomi-, machi-, hanashi-, aruki-); suru to shi-; kuru to ki-. Naming it converts twenty later 'grammar points' into ONE operation plus twenty tails. Note ki- from kuru vs ki- from kiru (wear) — kimasu is genuinely ambiguous, resolved by the object.
ACCENT: on ma. nomimásu, ikimásu, tabemásu. This is the one that obeys the naive rule.

ACCENT: on the na of -nagara. nominagara [3], arukinagara [4], tabenagara [3]. The -nagara clause is the BACKGROUND action; the main verb carries the point.

ACCENT: i-adjective penultimate rule, on the su. yomiyasui [4], tabeyasui [4], wakariyasui [5].
ACCENT: penultimate, on the ku. yominikui [4], tabenikui [4]. Taught in the same session as -yasui — they are one antonym pair, not two items.

gloss: the second shelf: plain negative and everything built on it
note: Ichidan: drop -ru, add -nai. Godan: -u to -a, add -nai. suru to shinai, kuru to konai, aru to NAI. Later tenants of this shelf: -nakya, -naide, -nakute, passive, causative. Named now for the same reason the i-stem was.

ACCENT RULE, UNIFORM: the accent sits on the mora immediately before -nai (the na). nomanai [3], ikanai [3], matanai [3], hanasanai [4], asobanai [4], isoganai [4], wakaranai [4]. One rule, no exceptions in this set.
Drop -ru. tabenai [3], minai [2], nenai [2], okinai [3], dekinai [3]. Same penult-na accent.

kana: かわない、いわない、おもわない、すわない
gloss: plain negative of verbs ending VOWEL + u
note: THE RULE STATED CORRECTLY: any verb whose dictionary form ends in VOWEL + u — that is -au, -iu, -ou, -uu — takes -wanai. kau/kawanai [3], YUU/IWANAI [3], omou/omowanai [4], suu/suwanai [3], au/awanai [3], morau/morawanai [4], tsukau/tsukawanai [4], narau/narawanai [4], warau/warawanai [4]. THE CONVENTIONAL STATEMENT SAYS '-au' AND THEREFORE MIS-GENERATES FOR YUU, one of the highest-frequency verbs in speech. Card the four vowel shapes, not one.

DOUBLE IRREGULARITY, CARDED SEPARATELY BECAUSE IT IS TWO SURPRISES AT ONCE: yuu takes -wanai (rule), AND its stem reverts to i- rather than yu- (memorized). yuu / yutte / yutta / IWANAI / iimasu. Never *yuwanai, never *yuanai.
suru to shinai. Memorized. Not to be confused with shinanai [3] (shinu, item 34) — a real and grim minimal pair, deliberately introduced on different days.
kuru to konai — the stem vowel changes to o, which happens nowhere else. Memorized. Some references list [1]; VERIFY against NHK at the recording pass and pick one for the whole deck.
ACCENT: on the ka. ikanakatta [4], tabenakatta [4], nomanakatta [4], hanasanakatta [5]. Standalone nakatta is [1].

gloss: -masu is the PRODUCTION default for the first four months; plain is what you HEAR
note: Stated explicitly so the learner does not treat the two as free variants. Produce -masu, comprehend both. The plain forms are stocked now because block E's contractions all attach to them.
Takes NO particle. mainichi hatarakimasu, never *mainichi ni. The natural partner of the habitual dictionary form.
Long vowel doubled. With affirmative past = already.
The 'not yet' sense needs a negative, and its most natural form is mada tabetenai — deferred to block E. Here only the affirmative 'still'.
POLARITY ITEM: ungrammatical without a negative. Colloquial anmari [0] taught as a variant.

kana: ぜんぜんわかりません
note: POLARITY ITEM. Two moraic N in four morae — a deliberate mora-timing workout as well as a word. ze-N-ze-N.
Adverbial form of ii/yoi. Frequency sense with habitual verbs.
From hayai [2]; the -ku form shifts to [1]. Card the shift, it recurs across i-adjectives.
Also sugu ni. All-CV, 2 morae — a cheap card.

kana: いっしょにいきましょう
note: Geminate doubled: i-Q-sho, 3 morae, sho is one mora. The default partner of -mashoo and -masen ka.

kana: あとででんわおします
note: Contrast with sugu. The 'after X' use (X no ato de) is previewed only.
From yasumu. Same point as hanashi.
i-stem + mono. Verify [2] vs [3] at the recording pass and apply the same choice to nomimono.
Geminate + long vowel: ga-Q-ko-o, 4 morae.
sha is ONE mora (yoon). sha-tsu = 2 morae, no geminate despite looking like one.
Paired with tabemono in one session — one operation, two words.

gloss: I don't understand / I don't know
note: Accent on se, consistent with -masen. Six morae. The single most useful sentence the learner can own in week 7 — carded whole, then re-derived from wakaru once the shell is drilled.

Accent on se. Contrast with wakarimasen: shirimasen = the fact is not in my head; wakarimasen = I can't make sense of it. Affirmative is NOT shirimasu but shitte imasu / shitteru (block E) — flag the asymmetry now.

gloss: what are you going to do?
note: wh-word + particle + shell. Drilled as a frame with a swappable head.
Contrast pair with doko ni. doko de = where do you do it; doko ni = where is it / where are you going.
Carries the clock-time ni. na-N-ji, 3 morae.
Completes the wh + particle set: nani o, doko de, doko ni, nan-ji ni, dare to, doko kara.

kana: かく、かいて。きく、きいて。いく、いって。
gloss: every verb enters memory as two sounds, never one
audioText: kaku, kaite. kiku, kiite. iku, itte.
note: THE CLOSING AUDIT ITEM. Recited daily. By day 56 the learner holds 65 pairs; the -te chant in block E is then a description of something already in the ear, not a rule to apply. The three-item audioText is deliberate: two regular -ku pairs then the exception, so iku is heard as odd rather than learned as odd.

kana: たべる、たべて。みる、みて。おきる、おきて。ねる、ねて。
gloss: CHANT ROW 0. Drop -ru, add -te. Zero segment change.
audioText: taberu, tabete. miru, mite. okiru, okite. neru, nete.
note: Opens the chant. The true one-to-one row: the ichidan stem is already isolated from the -masu shell in wk 6-7, so -te merely occupies a slot.
ACCENT LAW: -te keeps the dictionary accent index. Teach once, applies to all 60 verbs.
ite vs itte is the cleanest one-word gemination contrast the learner now owns. Feed it to the perception drill.
Pre-loads day 8, -te kureru.
New lexeme, budgeted. Named in the brief for R0, and the workhorse object of -te kureru and -te morau on days 8 and 10.
New lexeme, budgeted.
New lexeme, budgeted. Required by day 9: wasurechatta is the highest-frequency -chatta token in the language.

kana: はなす、はなして。かす、かして。だす、だして。なおす、なおして。
gloss: CHANT ROW 1. One-to-one, zero sound change.
audioText: hanasu, hanashite. kasu, kashite. dasu, dashite. naosu, naoshite.
note: This is literally the i-stem they already own from wk 6-7: hanashi- plus te. Perception load nil. NEVER drilled alone - R2 follows in the same session.
Keep at least 6 indices from kaette (n59): kaeshite and kaette are a transitivity pair AND a near-collision.

kana: かく、かいて。きく、きいて。あるく、あるいて。はたらく、はたらいて。
gloss: CHANT ROW 2. One-to-one. The consonant drops to a fully voiced vowel.
audioText: kaku, kaite. kiku, kiite. aruku, aruite. hataraku, hataraite.
note: Every mora carries acoustic energy - the easiest change row to hear. iku is EXCLUDED from this induction set and is not shown until day 4.

THREE morae, ki-i-te. Collides with kite [1] and kitte [1]/[0]. Vowel length is the cue; the whole triple is framed on day 13. COLLISION SET: identical to another -te form by ear. Disambiguated by argument frame (o-marked sound -> kiku), never by spacing — these are carded deliberately adjacent as a discrimination set.
Silent parent of -toku in wk 11. Do not mention the contraction yet.

kana: たべて、たべた。かいて、かいた。はなして、はなした。
gloss: PLAIN PAST. Identical slot, final vowel e > a. Costs nothing.
audioText: tabete, tabeta. kaite, kaita. hanashite, hanashita.
note: SHIPS IN THE SAME SESSION AS THE CHANT, every row, no exceptions. Deferring -ta is the largest unforced error available in this part of the course: it is one vowel swap and it buys -ta, -tara, -tari, -tatte, -ta koto ga aru, -ta hoo ga ii, -ta ato de and -ta bakari.

kana: たべた。みた。おしえた。でかけた。
note: Accent index preserved from the dictionary form, same law as -te.

kana: はなした。かした。だした。
かいた。きいた。あるいた。
note: kiita is four morae, ki-i-ta. Contrast with kita [1] from kuru on day 13.

kana: あさおきて、ごはんおたべた。
note: Highest-scoring node in the whole tree. Tense is carried by the FINAL clause only - the -te clause is tenseless. That is the hardest idea here for an English speaker and it is worth a card of its own.

kana: およぐ、およいで。いそぐ、いそいで。ぬぐ、ぬいで。さわぐ、さわいで。
gloss: CHANT ROW 3. One-to-one, voiced twin of R2.
audioText: oyogu, oyoide. isogu, isoide. nugu, nuide. sawagu, sawaide.
note: Drilled ADJACENT to R2 so ku/gu is learned as one contrast, not two rules. Only about five common members exist - say so, so the learner does not go hunting.
Doubles as the frozen adverb 'quickly, in a hurry'. That is the manner-junctive card on day 2.
accent approximate

kana: およいだ。いそいだ。ぬいだ。
note: VOICED past, -ida not *-ita. First appearance of the de > da half of the -ta rule.

kana: いそいでてがみおかいた。
gloss: 'by -ing', 'in an X way' - the -te clause says HOW
note: Same form, second reading, taught the day after sequence so -te does not fossilise as 'and then' only. Prosody is the cue: manner -te binds tight with no pause, sequence -te takes a pause.

kana: のむ、のんで。よむ、よんで。よぶ、よんで。あそぶ、あそんで。
gloss: CHANT ROW 4. FIRST MANY-TO-ONE. Cue is an AUDIBLE SEGMENT.
audioText: nomu, nonde. yomu, yonde. yobu, yonde. asobu, asonde.
note: Drilled as TWO codas, -mu and -bu, with shinde attached separately as a lexical item. shinu is the only -nu verb; one member cannot support induction and presenting it as a class invites a hunt for verbs that do not exist. The cue is a moraic nasal plus voicing on the /d/ - both have sound in them. NEVER in the same session as R5.
MINIMAL PAIR with n43 yonde from yobu [0]. Pitch separates them, but only if the audio runs at least 4 morae past the verb so the contour is recoverable.
ALWAYS framed with an obligatory locative: ie ni sunde. Pitch does NOT reliably separate it from sunde 'finish', which stays deferred at least 6 weeks.
The other yonde, heiban. Carded three indices after the [1] member and always with an animate object, so semantics backs up the pitch.

pos: LEXICAL ATTACHMENT to R4, not a class
note: The ONLY -nu verb in the language. Taught as one word, never as a row.

kana: のんだ。よんだ。あそんだ。しんだ。
note: de > da. Voiced throughout.

kana: かう、かって。まつ、まって。とる、とって。つかう、つかって。
gloss: CHANT ROW 5. MANY-TO-ONE and the cue is A BEAT OF SILENCE.
audioText: kau, katte. matsu, matte. toru, totte. tsukau, tsukatte.
note: LAST of the rule rows. Three codas collapse to one output AND the only acoustic evidence is a mora with no energy in it - the hardest thing an audio-only ear does. Gets the longest session in the block. iku is not in this induction set either; it is appended afterwards as a defector.

Heiban. Anchors R5 and anchors the H4 collision set. COLLISION SET: identical to another -te form by ear. Disambiguated by argument frame (o-marked goods -> kau), never by spacing — these are carded deliberately adjacent as a discrimination set.

CORRECTION APPLIED: au is [1], NOT [0]. Its -te form atte is therefore HL and ACCENT-IDENTICAL to atte from aru [1]. The earlier pass's pitch-separation claim for this pair is FALSE and is withdrawn here. Separate them by argument structure instead: tomodachi ni atte (dative animate) vs kagi ga atte (nominative inanimate). COLLISION SET: identical to another -te form by ear. Disambiguated by argument frame (ni-marked person -> au [1]), never by spacing — these are carded deliberately adjacent as a discrimination set.
Becomes the single most-used token of week 9 - chotto matte.
Frame obligatorily: te de totte. Pitch does NOT separate it from tootte (tooru) - vowel length is the only cue, and tooru stays deferred at least 6 weeks.
The -eru/-iru trap set. The geminate proves the class.
Feeds wakatte kita on day 11, the model inchoative.

ACCENT-IDENTICAL to atte from au [1]. Separated by argument frame only: kagi ga atte. COLLISION SET: identical to another -te form by ear. Disambiguated by argument frame (ni-marked location -> aru [1]), never by spacing — these are carded deliberately adjacent as a discrimination set.
Pre-loads day 10.
New lexeme, budgeted. The canonical object of -te kureru and -te morau.
New lexeme, budgeted. Needed for suwatte ii? on day 12.

THE SINGLE MOST-CITED OMISSION FROM THE EARLIER PASS, fixed here. iu is PRONOUNCED yuu; card it as yuu, past yutta, -teru yutteta. Not stylistic - it DISSOLVES the itte collision, because yutta vs itta is genuinely audible and the past is where most of this verb's tokens live. It also removes the near-collision between the citation forms iu and iku. itte 'say' stays passive recognition only and is never produced.

SELL THIS TO THE LEARNER: kaette vs kaete is the only AUDIBLE godan/ichidan test that exists for -ru verbs. The chant is a class diagnostic. The ichidan partner kaete is withheld until day 13. COLLISION SET: identical to another -te form by ear. Disambiguated by argument frame (ni-marked home -> kaeru godan), never by spacing — these are carded deliberately adjacent as a discrimination set.

kana: あしたくるってゆった。
note: Carded here because tte yutteta is a top-20 conversational chunk and is unbuildable without yuu.

romaji: R6: IRREGULARS - two words, not a row
gloss: suru > shite, kuru > kite. Memorised, not induced.
note: Placed after every rule row has closed, precisely so the learner cannot mistake them for a row and induce a pattern that does not exist. Label them out loud as exceptions.

Contrast pair with shitte (n62) IN THIS SESSION. The pair that actually costs points is shiteru vs shitteru on day 5. COLLISION SET: identical to another -te form by ear. Disambiguated by argument frame (o-marked task -> suru), never by spacing — these are carded deliberately adjacent as a discrimination set.

Accented [1], H-L. That integer is load-bearing: it is the only thing separating it from kite [0] (kiru 'wear', day 13) once meaning is stripped. VERIFY with a native voice, do not guess. COLLISION SET: identical to another -te form by ear. Disambiguated by argument frame (ni-marked goal -> motion verb), never by spacing — these are carded deliberately adjacent as a discrimination set.

romaji: iku > ITTE - THE SOLE GODAN EXCEPTION
kana: いく、いって。いく、いった。
gloss: iku takes -tte, not *iite. One verb, no class.
note: Deliberately KEPT OUT of the R2 induction set and shown three days after R2 closed, so -ku > -ite is stable before its defector appears. Framed as 'iku defects into the -tte row'. If the learner ever produces *iite, stop the mix and re-block R2 for one full session.

romaji: katta / matta / totta / itta / shita / kita
kana: かった。まった。とった。いった。した。きた。
gloss: R5, R6 and iku past forms
audioText: katta. matta. totta. itta. shita. kita.
note: itta [0] from iku and itta [0] from yuu are both heiban and identical. Pitch separates nothing. This is exactly why yutta is the production citation.

gloss: DURATIVE verb + -teru = doing it right now
note: CITATION IS -teru, NOT -te iru. -te iru is taught in the same session but labelled the formal expansion, never the primary. The two readings are CO-TAUGHT in one session and keyed on the verb's aktionsart; teaching them sequentially installs a default that is then wrong half the time.
Carded inside the question frame - that is where most of its tokens are.

kana: せんせいとはなしてる。

gloss: PUNCTUAL or CHANGE-OF-STATE verb + -teru = the state that resulted
note: THE KEY IS THE VERB, NOT THE CONTEXT. Give the learner the test out loud: does the verb name something that takes time (tabe-, hanashi-, mat-, aruk-) or something instantaneous that leaves a state behind (shir-, mots-, sum-, ak-, kekkon)? Durative gives progressive, punctual gives state. One rule with one diagnostic, not two homonymous constructions.

gloss: knows (state of having come to know)
note: Minimal pair with shiteru [0] - identical pitch, one extra beat of silence. Deliberately co-carded on the same day as its partner so gemination is the trained cue rather than an avoided one.
Obligatory locative in the frame, always.
New lexeme, budgeted. The clearest change-of-state exemplar: aku is instantaneous, so -teru can only mean the resulting state.

kana: あねわけっこんしてる。
note: New lexeme, budgeted, carded ONLY in this 5-mora collocation frame per the kango rule - never bare. Also the sharpest proof of reading 2 for an English speaker, who will otherwise hear 'is getting married'.
accent approximate. Formal expansion -te inai taught as a label only.

kana: さっきまでざっしおよんでた。
gloss: was -ing / had been in the state
note: accent approximate. -te ita is the labelled formal expansion.
accent approximate.

kana: なにしてるの？なにしてんの？
audioText: nani shiteru no? nani shiten no?
note: BOTH forms on one card. -ten no? is what actually occurs in the stream; -teru no? is the slower variant. The contracted one is the primary.

kana: あのひとのなまえ、しらない。
note: FLAGGED: shitteru's negative is shiranai, NOT *shittenai and NOT *shitte inai. Card it as a distinct lexical item on the same day as -tenai, or the learner builds it wrong and it fossilises. This is the one place -tenai does not apply.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the earlier pass, which deferred shiru to wk 13. shitteru is required by the -teru resultant-state session on day 5 and that session is unbuildable without it. Mitigation: shite and shitte are introduced in the SAME session as an explicitly contrasted pair with an obligatory 4+ mora tail, so gemination is trained rather than dodged, and the H3 perception drill already ran in wks 1-2. COLLISION SET: identical to another -te form by ear. Disambiguated by argument frame (always -teru; bare shitte is ungrammatical), never by spacing — these are carded deliberately adjacent as a discrimination set.

kana: ちょっとまってください。
pos: construction, slot 3, F6 x Q8 = 48 (promoted by TB1)
note: kudasai is [3]. Promoted above its raw score because a learner who cannot make a request cannot hold a conversation.
Carded WITH -te kudasai, not after it. In the target register the bare form is by far the more frequent, so it is the unmarked member and the polite one is marked.

kana: まだたべないでください。
note: REACHES ACROSS STEMS DELIBERATELY. The negative request takes the -nai stem from wk 8, not -te. If it is not carded in the same session as -te kudasai the learner produces *-te nai kudasai. Two cards, and it closes the request paradigm.
kureru [0]. Direction is inward and fixed: the subject is someone else, the beneficiary is me. State it as a rule, do not leave it to examples.

kana: せんせいがおしえてくれた。
note: ga marks the doer. Hold this against the morau frame on day 10.

kana: ちょっとまってくれない？
gloss: won't you do X for me? (softened request)
note: Explain that the negative here is politeness, not negation, or it is heard as a complaint.

kana: かさ、かしてくれませんか。
gloss: would you do X for me? (polite)

kana: たべて、たべちゃう。よんで、よんじゃう。かって、かっちゃう。のんで、のんじゃう。
gloss: the completive / regret contraction, BOTH members
audioText: tabete, tabechau. yonde, yonjau. katte, katchau. nonde, nonjau.
note: THE VOICED MEMBER WAS MISSING FROM AN EARLIER PASS - a fatal defect, fixed here. The rule is stated ONCE and generally: a -te ending gives -chau, a -de ending gives -jau. Say out loud that the same voiced/voiceless split governs -toku/-doku, -tara/-dara and -cha/-ja dame in weeks 11-12, so the learner pays for the alternation once and collects three times.

gloss: do it completely / end up doing it
note: Accent falls on the cha mora. Citation is -chau, not -te shimau; the long form is a labelled formal expansion only.

gloss: went and did it (regret / completion, past)
note: Higher frequency than the non-past. Lead the session with this one - wasurechatta alone earns the card.

kana: そのざっし、きょうよんじゃう。
note: Never card -chau without -jau in the same session. Zero *yonchau tolerated in drill.

kana: コーヒーのんじゃった。

note: Proves the split is conditioned by the -de ending, not by verb class.

kana: あににてつだってもらう。
gloss: get someone to do X for me (receive a favour)
note: morau [0]. THE SUBJECT IS ME. That is the whole difference from -te kureru and it must be drilled as a swap, not learned as two separate facts.

kana: せんせいにおしえてもらった。
gloss: got someone to do X for me

kana: ちょっとみてもらえる？
gloss: could I get you to do X? (casual polite request)

kana: ともだちがかしてくれた。ともだちにかしてもらった。
gloss: same event, flipped subject: X ga ...-te kureta = X ni ...-te moratta
audioText: tomodachi ga kashite kureta. tomodachi ni kashite moratta.
note: Note the particle flip, ga vs ni. English collapses both into one sentence, so this must be a swap drill or the learner picks one and never uses the other.

gloss: go do X and come back
note: kuru [1]. Two unrelated senses, TWO cards, both in this session.

gloss: went and did X and came back
has started to / is coming to be
note: Sense 2 is keyed on the verb again: a motion verb gives the directional reading, a cognition or change verb gives the inchoative. Same aktionsart diagnostic the learner built for -teru - say so explicitly, it is the second payoff for one idea.

gloss: has come to be, has started

note: New lexeme, budgeted. ame ga futte kita is the model inchoative token.

gloss: go get X / go do X and come back (request)
note: First stacked construction: two -te forms in one clause. Flag that only the LAST verb carries the request.

pos: construction, slot 8, F4 x Q7 = 28 (PROMOTED by TB1)
note: Promoted above four higher-scoring nodes because a learner who cannot ask permission cannot function. ii is [1].
The mo drops in casual speech. This is the form in the stream, so it is carded as an equal, not as a footnote.

kana: このぺんつかってもいいよ。
audioText: kono pen tsukatte mo ii yo.
note: The learner must be able to RECOGNISE permission being granted, not only request it.

kana: きょうわこなくてもいい。
note: Second deliberate cross-stem reach, same reason as -naide kudasai: permission-not-to takes the -nai stem, and if it is not carded beside -te mo ii the learner builds *-te nai mo ii.
Same onbin slot as -te, final vowel e>a. Costs nothing once the chant exists.

H1. HEIBAN [0], L-H, against kite [1] H-L from kuru. The accent integer is the ONLY phonological cue and must be verified with a native voice, not guessed. Non-phonological cue supplied by the frame: a garment noun licenses only the wear reading. RECOG only in this block; production opens wk 12 per the separation rule. COLLISION SET: identical to another -te form by ear. Disambiguated by argument frame (o-marked garment -> kiru ichidan), never by spacing — these are carded deliberately adjacent as a discrimination set.

gloss: 'is there a stamp?' - the NOUN kitte [0] in a verb-shaped slot
